A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WizardMath and RLEIF. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original WizardMath evaluations on GSM8k, MATH and MWPBench, together with reward-model ablations, data-scaling experiments and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds an experiment using Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct to label PRM training data.

M1.justification: The instruction-evolution procedure, IRM and PRM objectives, reward combination, PPO training and verification remain unchanged. New Appendix A.6 explains the existing pipeline; the alternative PRM annotator is tested within that pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8k, MATH and the same seven MWPBench out-of-domain tasks. The added base-model and annotator comparisons use existing benchmarks without expanding task or population coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 16 adds untreated Mathstral-7B, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and Qwen2.5-7B comparators; Qwen2.5-Math-7B was already included in v2 Table 14. Table 19 adds a Llama-3.1-405B-labeled PRM variant alongside the GPT-4-labeled PRM and SFT baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix A.12 adds a controlled annotator comparison using Llama-3.1-405B instead of GPT-4, with Mistral-7B and the same stated labeling prompts and training settings. Existing benchmark splits and metrics are retained; A.7's additional settings document comparisons already present in v2 and do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New A.12/Table 19 tests sensitivity to the model providing PRM annotations. Existing evolution-turn, reward-component, data-scaling, verification and out-of-domain analyses remain; the expanded discussion of DART-Math comparisons mostly concerns evidence already in v2.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without documented independent repeated runs, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 19 newly reports 85.8% GSM8k and 51.5% MATH for the Llama-labeled PRM, compared with retained GPT-4-labeled results of 87.2% and 52.7%. Table 16 adds three previously unreported base-model rows. Matched existing tables retain their scores, although new A.9 prose incorrectly gives 48.9 where Table 17 retains 48.7.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(4), defining the reward-model losses, combined reward and answer aggregation, are unchanged. The added pipeline explanation introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain their central method and performance claims. New Appendix A.13 strengthens novelty positioning through explicit first-to-propose claims for downward evolution, combined IRM/PRM training and AI annotation of step-level PRM data.

C2.justification: The new appendix discussion qualifies SFT performance against Xwin-Math and Skywork-Math through data-efficiency tradeoffs and discusses gains on math-specialized backbones. A.12 explicitly acknowledges GPT-4 labeling costs and the lack of ground-truth answers needed by Math-Shepherd, interpreting the alternative annotator as a potential cost-accuracy compromise.

D1.justification: A.7 adds comparison-specific training details, including four checkpoints per epoch and selection by highest GSM8k/MATH accuracy. Its reported batch size of 256 is not reconciled with Section 4.1's 512. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish changed execution or resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 removes the extended related-work appendix and many distinct references across language modeling, mathematical reasoning and reinforcement learning, including QLoRA, Orca-Math and MathCoder. Section 2 remains largely intact, while new appendix passages sharpen comparisons with data-synthesis methods and make explicit priority claims.

P1.justification: The appendix undergoes substantial narrative reorganization: the extended survey is replaced by a detailed pipeline walkthrough, existing comparisons receive extensive explanation, and previously heading-only subsections gain substantive prose. The main text receives only limited wording, cross-reference and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 16 and 19, relocates Figure 4 beside the contamination discussion, and redistributes and renumbers existing appendix tables. Figure 1 gains an explanatory cross-reference, while existing graphics and table formats remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes previously unexplained appendix comparisons easier to assess, discloses checkpoint-selection details, and adds useful PRM-annotator evidence and explicit limitations. These provide a modest net benefit because the main method and existing results remain unchanged. Reduced literature coverage and new consistency errors, including A.9's 48.9 versus Table 17's 48.7 and the incorrect Table 19 reference in Section 4.3, temper the improvement.
